title: Why In-Camera Presets Aren't Cheating
excerpt: Fujifilm's film simulations, custom recipes on OM System and Nikon — Digital Camera World's Mike Harris argues in-camera presets aren't cheating. They teach exposure discipline, kill editing anxiety, and keep you shooting instead of sitting at a screen.

title: Your Stabilization Rating Comes From a Shaker Table, Not a Hand
excerpt: Your camera's stabilization rating comes from a shaker table in a temperature-controlled room, not a human hand. The test is rigorous, but the focal length and lens are the manufacturer's choice — so 8.5 stops and 7.5 stops are not reliably a stop apart.

title: How to Find Compositions When the Location Overwhelms You
excerpt: Omar Gonzalez fought the tourist-snapshot trap in Vermont and won. His answer: compositional blinders — the viewfinder, a long lens, or a crop mode that forces your eye to find the frame.
